import pandas as pd

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length3_14/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length3_14/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length3_14/training_2.csv", index_col=0)

# Step 1: Join Source1 and Source2 on 'user_id'
join_1_2 = pd.merge(source1, source2, on="user_id", how="inner")

# Step 2: Join the result with Source0 on 'movie_id'
final_join = pd.merge(join_1_2, source0[['movie_id', 'title']], on="movie_id", how="inner")

# Select and reorder columns to match target schema:
# ['title': string, 'user_id': float, 'movie_id': integer, 'rating': float, 'timestamp': float, 'age': float, 'occupation': float]

# Ensure correct dtypes:
final_join['title'] = final_join['title'].astype(str)
final_join['user_id'] = final_join['user_id'].astype(float)
final_join['movie_id'] = final_join['movie_id'].astype(int)
final_join['rating'] = final_join['rating'].astype(float)
final_join['timestamp'] = final_join['timestamp'].astype(float)
final_join['age'] = final_join['age'].astype(float)
final_join['occupation'] = final_join['occupation'].astype(float)

# Reorder columns
Target3_14 = final_join[['title', 'user_id', 'movie_id', 'rating', 'timestamp', 'age', 'occupation']]

# Write the result to the specified path without the index
Target3_14.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_14/target_multisource.csv", index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_14/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_14/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_14/training_2.csv", index_col=0)

# Join Source1 and Source2 on user_id
joined_1_2 = pd.merge(source1, source2, on="user_id", how="inner")

# Join Source0 and the above join on movie_id
joined_all = pd.merge(source0, joined_1_2, on="movie_id", how="inner")

# Group by the leftmost non-float columns in target schema: title (string), user_id (float but used as group key), movie_id (int)
# Aggregate other columns by mean as target examples show averages
result = joined_all.groupby(["title", "user_id", "movie_id"], as_index=False).agg({
    "rating": "mean",
    "timestamp": "mean",
    "age": "mean",
    "occupation": "mean"
})

# Ensure column order and types match target schema exactly
result = result[["title", "user_id", "movie_id", "rating", "timestamp", "age", "occupation"]]

# Write to target file
result.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_14/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
